name: Tilon
overview: Tilon is a male figure from the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Shimon. His mention in Scripture is brief and primarily genealogical, with no additional notes or narrative details provided. This places him within the broader context of Judah's lineage as recorded in 1 Chronicles.
namesAndTitles: The name Tilon appears as a proper name in Scripture without an explicit meaning or divine origin noted. There is only one recorded instance of this name in 1 Chronicles 4:20, and no further significance is attributed to it in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Tilon as the son of Shimon, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical record for Tilon.
scriptureSignificance: Tilon's significance lies in his inclusion in the genealogical records of the tribe of Judah, which is foundational for understanding the lineage of God's chosen people. Though not prominent in narrative events, his mention underscores the importance of preserving tribal heritage and ancestry in Scripture. This genealogical detail contributes to the comprehensive biblical framework that traces God's providential work through generations.
